root_cause.text: The amdgpu PCI probe incorrectly used the global `amdgpu_aspm` setting to mirror `pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)` for the currently probed device, so on multi-GPU systems one GPU’s lack of ASPM support could disable ASPM handling globally and corrupt per-device ASPM behavior for another GPU.
root_cause.evidence: The reverted code in `amdgpu_pci_probe()` set `amdgpu_aspm = 0` when `amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)`, and the commit message states this was wrongly reintroduced after ASPM had been refactored “to be evaluated per device,” causing crashes “with a system with two AMD GPUs of which only one supports ASPM.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop amdgpu_pci_probe() from automatically disabling amdgpu_aspm when PCIe ASPM is disabled by the system.
intent_record.what: A conditional block was removed from amdgpu_pci_probe() that checked whether amdgpu_aspm was -1 and PCIe ASPM was disabled for the device, and if so assigned amdgpu_aspm = 0.
intent_record.how: The probe path no longer forces the global amdgpu_aspm setting to disabled when system PCIe ASPM is off and amdgpu_aspm is still in its default auto state, allowing the variable to remain unchanged and preventing automatic override during device initialization.

grouping_result.intent: Stop amdgpu_pci_probe() from automatically disabling amdgpu_aspm when PCIe ASPM is disabled by the system.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly removes the probe-time behavior that overwrote the global amdgpu_aspm setting based on PCIe ASPM state, which is the root cause of incorrect global/per-device ASPM handling on multi-GPU systems.

candidates.rationale: This assignment mutates the global amdgpu_aspm setting based on the ASPM state of the currently probed device, causing one GPU's probe result to disable ASPM handling globally for other GPUs.
This condition ties the global amdgpu_aspm policy to pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev) for a single probed device, which is the root of the incorrect per-device-to-global coupling on multi-GPU systems.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement is the direct global state mutation that causes the vulnerability: it disables the global amdgpu_aspm setting based on the ASPM status of the currently probed device, breaking correct per-device ASPM behavior on multi-GPU systems.

This conditional is the control point that incorrectly couples a per-device PCIe ASPM check to the global amdgpu_aspm policy, enabling the subsequent global disable when probing a device without ASPM support.

bic_trace_step.reason: The shown function body is sufficient because the relevant ASPM probe logic is explicitly present in the diff. The vulnerable construct is the newly added global assignment: `if (amdgpu_aspm == -1 && !pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)) amdgpu_aspm = 0;`. Per the root cause, the bug is using the global `amdgpu_aspm` setting to mirror `pcie_aspm_enabled(pdev)` for the currently probed device. That is exactly what this code does: it checks ASPM status for one `pdev` and then writes the result into the global `amdgpu_aspm`. On a multi-GPU system, probing one GPU with ASPM disabled can force `amdgpu_aspm = 0` globally and affect other devices incorrectly. The proper fix would avoid storing per-device PCIe ASPM state in a global knob; this snippet still performs that global update, so the vulnerable construct is present and the fix is not yet present.
